CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In art, tone or value means (1 mark)
   A. how old it is
   B. how loud it is
   C. how big it is
   D. how light or dark something is

2. What is the first step in improvising an accompaniment to a song? (1 mark)
   A. Find the steady beat
   B. Change the words
   C. Buy a drum
   D. Stop singing

3. Smudging a charcoal drawing means (1 mark)
   A. rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   B. folding the paper
   C. painting over it
   D. erasing it completely

4. What is the minimum distance a defender must keep from the player with the ball? (1 mark)
   A. 0.9 metres
   B. 10 metres
   C. 1 centimetre
   D. 5 metres

5. How long may a player hold the ball before passing or shooting? (1 mark)
   A. As long as they like
   B. Ten seconds
   C. Three seconds
   D. One minute

6. The first step of tying an overhand knot is to (1 mark)
   A. cut the cord
   B. burn the cord
   C. wet the cord
   D. make a loop

7. Which is a rule break in netball? (1 mark)
   A. Catching with two hands
   B. Pushing another player
   C. Passing to a teammate
   D. Pivoting on one foot

8. Where do you place a soft shadow when painting a fruit on a table? (1 mark)
   A. On the table under the fruit
   B. On the ceiling
   C. Inside the fruit
   D. Nowhere

9. Repeating a small group of notes in a rhythm helps listeners to (1 mark)
   A. forget the pattern
   B. stop listening
   C. change the words
   D. remember the pattern

10. The recorder notes G, A and B match the sol-fa syllables (1 mark)
   A. m, d and r
   B. r, m and d
   C. d, r and m
   D. m, r and d

11. The home note of the melodies in this lesson is (1 mark)
   A. d
   B. m
   C. r
   D. none of them

12. In a good sprinting technique, the elbows are bent to about (1 mark)
   A. a tiny angle
   B. a right angle
   C. a straight line
   D. a full circle

13. Which is a sprint distance in big athletics competitions? (1 mark)
   A. 100 metres
   B. Marathon
   C. Half marathon
   D. 10 000 metres

14. The middle stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. black
   B. green
   C. red
   D. blue

15. Where should you stay during a sprint race? (1 mark)
   A. On the grass beside the track
   B. Across all lanes
   C. In your own lane
   D. In any lane

16. How should we treat the national flag? (1 mark)
   A. With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground
   B. Use it as a rag
   C. Write on it
   D. Throw it around

17. Why do we stand up slowly after a side roll? (1 mark)
   A. To look tall
   B. To avoid feeling dizzy
   C. To win a prize
   D. To make noise

18. If your head drops back with a strain in the crab balance, you should (1 mark)
   A. hold your breath
   B. throw it back further
   C. keep the head in line and look gently up
   D. close your mouth tight

19. At the start of the side roll, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. folded on your chest
   B. stretched above your head
   C. behind your back
   D. on your knees

20. At a wedding, we are most likely to hear (1 mark)
   A. marriage songs
   B. work songs only
   C. funeral songs
   D. topical songs only

21. Pitch is (1 mark)
   A. how loud it is
   B. how fast it is
   C. how high or low a note is
   D. the words

22. A song that is played fast has a (1 mark)
   A. soft dynamic
   B. long title
   C. fast tempo
   D. low pitch

23. What should you do about distracting things behind the subject? (1 mark)
   A. Add more
   B. Ignore them always
   C. Remove them or change the angle
   D. Photograph them too

24. On the staff, the note G sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 2
   B. the top line
   C. a space above the staff
   D. line 3

25. Where should you walk beside the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Jumping
   B. Running
   C. Sliding
   D. On the pool side, walking slowly

26. Who can teach you an indigenous game from your community? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger online
   B. Nobody
   C. An elder
   D. Only a computer

27. Before animal games you should (1 mark)
   A. eat a big meal
   B. sleep
   C. warm up
   D. fight

28. Every displayed work should have (1 mark)
   A. a label with the title and artist's name
   B. a secret code
   C. a price only
   D. no name

29. Which are instrumentalists in a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. Dancers only
   B. People playing drums or shakers
   C. The audience
   D. The umpire

30. Works on display should be kept away from (1 mark)
   A. shelves
   B. other pictures
   C. walls
   D. water, direct sun and dust

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why is it important to appreciate the percussion instruments of different communities? (3 marks)

32. How can you show the mood of a joyful song when singing? (3 marks)

33. Why does a drum sound higher when its skin is tightened? (3 marks)

34. Describe how to make a portfolio from manila paper. (5 marks)

35. Name any two players' positions in netball. (2 marks)

36. Describe the Kodaly hand sign for each of d, r and m. (3 marks)

37. State what the colours black and green stand for on the Kenyan flag. (2 marks)

38. What is the difference between a working portfolio and a display portfolio? (2 marks)

39. Why does a recorder squeak when you blow too hard? (2 marks)

40. Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio. (4 marks)

41. How should you behave when the Kenya National Anthem is sung? (3 marks)

42. Explain what is meant by two stars and a wish in feedback. (3 marks)

43. Give three responsible ways of using a device for photography. (3 marks)

44. What is the difference between tempo and dynamics? (2 marks)

45. How should we behave towards the national flag? (3 marks)

46. Explain the meaning of diction and why it matters. (3 marks)

47. Why is swimming an essential life skill? (2 marks)

48. Name two parts of a drum. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — how light or dark something is
   Tone is the lightness or darkness of a colour or shading.

2. A — Find the steady beat
   You must find the beat before you can add patterns.

3. A — rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   Smudging spreads the charcoal so that light and dark blend smoothly.

4. A — 0.9 metres
   A defender must stand at least 0.9 metres away.

5. C — Three seconds
   A player must pass or shoot within three seconds.

6. D — make a loop
   You make a loop first, pass the end through it and pull tight.

7. B — Pushing another player
   Contact such as pushing is not allowed.

8. A — On the table under the fruit
   A shadow under the object makes it seem to sit on the table.

9. D — remember the pattern
   Repetition gives shape and makes the rhythm easier to remember.

10. C — d, r and m
   If G is doh, then A is ray and B is me.

11. A — d
   Melodies feel finished when they end on d.

12. B — a right angle
   Bent arms swinging back and forth help the stride.

13. A — 100 metres
   The sprints are 100 m, 200 m and 400 m.

14. C — red
   Red is the middle stripe.

15. C — In your own lane
   Running in your lane prevents crashes.

16. A — With care and respect, never letting it touch the ground
   Respect for the flag means caring for it.

17. B — To avoid feeling dizzy
   Getting up too fast can make you dizzy.

18. C — keep the head in line and look gently up
   Keep the head in line with the body.

19. B — stretched above your head
   Arms overhead with palms together keep the body long.

20. A — marriage songs
   Marriage songs praise the couple and give good wishes.

21. C — how high or low a note is
   Accurate pitch means singing the right notes.

22. C — fast tempo
   Tempo is speed.

23. C — Remove them or change the angle
   A plain background keeps attention on the subject.

24. A — line 2
   G is on the second line from the bottom with the treble clef.

25. D — On the pool side, walking slowly
   Wet floors are slippery.

26. C — An elder
   Elders know many traditional games.

27. C — warm up
   Warming up prepares muscles.

28. A — a label with the title and artist's name
   Labels help viewers.

29. B — People playing drums or shakers
   Instrumentalists play instruments.

30. D — water, direct sun and dust
   Water, sun and dust can damage works.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show the culture and skill of each community. They help us respect one another. They should be preserved for future generations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Smile, use lively gestures, sing brightly and at a lively tempo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: A tighter skin vibrates faster. Faster vibration makes a higher sound. Ropes are used to tighten the skin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for faster vibration, 1 mark for higher sound, 1 mark for the ropes or tightening.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Fold two large pieces of manila paper to make a folder and trim the edges. Punch holes and add a string tie. Paste coloured paper or fabric on the cover. Write a label with name and class. Put in the works with dates and notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Goal Shooter, Goal Attack, Wing Attack, Centre, Wing Defence, Goal Defence, Goal Keeper. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: d is a closed fist, r is a sloping palm, m is a flat palm held level.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Black stands for the people of Kenya. Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: A working portfolio holds work in progress. A display portfolio holds the best finished works for showing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: The air is blown too strongly, so the note jumps to a very high shrill sound. Blow more gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight and still, face the flag, remove your cap, sing clearly and do not talk or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say two good things about the work and then give one suggestion for improvement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before photographing someone; do not photograph in private places; do not share photographs without permission; use it only for the set task. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tempo is the speed of the music. Dynamics are how loud or soft the music is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not let it touch the ground, do not write on it, keep it clean and not torn, and stand still and quiet when it is raised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Diction is saying the words clearly. It matters because the audience can understand the message of the song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drumhead (skin) and shell (body). Rope and beater are also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.
